name: McDonald's
headline: Collects rent and royalties on about 45,000 restaurants under 20-year contracts.
what_it_does: McDonald's franchises about 45,000 restaurants, of which 2,039 it runs itself. It owns or leases the land and buildings and collects rent and a royalty on sales: franchised revenues were $16.5 billion in 2025, of which rents were $10.4 billion and royalties $6.0 billion. Systemwide sales were $139.4 billion.
why_it_passed: Its cash is a share of what 45,000 restaurants sell, fixed by franchise agreements that usually run 20 years, with $31.5 billion of future minimum rents already contracted.
Its sites and drive-thrus cannot be copied with money alone, and the brand travels abroad.
It earns a high return on the capital it needs, and the increment still earns about 23% before tax.
No doubt about the honesty of management was raised by the documents read.
why_not_now: At $233.04 a share against a value range of $164 to $195, the price is above the top. A buyer would earn about 4.0% to 4.8% a year after tax on the cash the business produces, less than a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.66%). The analysis says the business is not the reason; the price is.
watch: Guest counts in the US are falling, and a rival reported an 8.5% quarter.
Capital spending is up 43% in two years and it announced $8.5 billion of support for franchisees, which has kept the cash the owners get flat for four years.
It has bought back shares, partly with borrowed money, at prices above any value the analysis can support, with no stated price discipline.
